sources_considered.why: Contemporaneous record of OpenAI's 80% price cut on o3, the same model, with before and after prices.
Anthropic's own announcement of $5/$25 pricing for Opus 4.5, down from the earlier Opus price of $15/$75.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI just dropped the price of their o3 model by 80% - from $10/million input tokens and $40/million output tokens to just $2/million and $8/million for the very same model.

evidence_items.explanation: Customers' price for the very same model fell 80%. That directly contradicts 'costs have only ever increased' for customers.

receipt.public_excerpt: Pricing is now $5/$25 per million tokens—making Opus-level capabilities accessible to even more users, teams, and enterprises.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic cut its Opus-tier API price to $5/$25 per million tokens, from the $15/$75 for Opus 4 recorded in e1's source. The price of top-tier Claude use fell by two-thirds.

inputs: Opus 4 price $15 input / $75 output per million tokens (simonwillison.net, 2025-06-10)
Opus 4.5 price $5 input / $25 output per million tokens (anthropic.com)

receipt.public_excerpt: Cost fell 390x in one year (o3's $4,500/task to GPT-5.2's $12/task), although this largely reflects reduced test-time parallelism.

evidence_items.explanation: Measured per-task cost on a benchmark fell sharply within a year. The authors note that the fall partly reflects less parallel compute.

evidence_items.locator: Live update, Oct 26, 2026, 3:53 PM UTC entry

receipt.public_excerpt: The cost of the computing power that runs its Claude models rose far less, to $5.6 billion from $3.4 billion.

evidence_items.explanation: A provider's total compute cost rose from Q1 to Q2 2026. That fits the total-spending reading of his claim, though it does not show that unit costs rose.

metric_scope.metric: compute cost (cost of computing power for Claude models)

unresolved_gaps: Provider unit inference costs (cost per token served) are not directly disclosed in the sources read.
Total customer spending may have risen as reasoning models use more tokens. That alternative reading is not settled here.
